lean-evidence-first-reasoning.name: lean-evidence-first-reasoning
lean-evidence-first-reasoning.title: Lean, evidence-first reasoning habits in the system prompt
lean-evidence-first-reasoning.what: Adds a short APPEND_SYSTEM.md section: think only as far as the next step; don't re-quote code already shown or draft code in reasoning; settle doubts by running code and printing actual values; check APIs in installed source and don't reconstruct uncheckable facts from memory at length; batch lookups; re-read your own code on unexpected failures; save slow test output to a file instead of re-running.
lean-evidence-first-reasoning.why: In the parent's 100 runs 69% of output tokens are thinking. Thinking blocks over 3k chars hold 60% of it, and 296 of those 404 blocks are recalling ('recall', 'from memory', 'I believe') rather than checking. 21% of thinking is in code fences, 45% of those lines copies of code already shown. 93% of turns make one tool call; 35 runs re-ran a test command just to filter output differently; repro scripts built on misremembered APIs and wrong hand-computed asserts cost many turns.
lean-evidence-first-reasoning.expect: Same solves with fewer output tokens, mostly by trimming long recall/tracing blocks and redundant turns in heavy runs. Text only, applies on every task (no kick-in count). On small trial repos: same fixes, verification kept, usually fewer tokens but noisy.

progress-check-notes.name: progress-check-notes
progress-check-notes.title: Progress checks: wrap-up note after passing tests, periodic stock-take
progress-check-notes.what: An extension appends a short progress check to tool results: when a test run passes after a source edit (at most twice per run), and at tool call 25 and every 15 calls after. Each lists the files changed so far (git status, or edited paths outside git) and asks the agent to finish if the request works, or else to name the gap in one sentence and go straight for it.
progress-check-notes.why: In parent runs, 16% of output came after the first passing test run that followed the last source edit (median 8 more turns of reruns and re-reading). 33% came after turn 30, in 53 of 100 runs. Long runs also lost track of their own edits: 3 runs decided their changes came 'from a previous session' or answered a 'second user message'; one wasted about 25 turns.
progress-check-notes.expect: Fewer turns once the fix works, so fewer output tokens on mid-length and long runs, with the same solves. Simulated on the parent's runs, the pass note fires in about 80% of runs and the periodic check in about 65%. Plain questions are unaffected.

skip-unrequested-tests-docs.name: skip-unrequested-tests-docs
skip-unrequested-tests-docs.title: Keep work to what was asked: no unrequested tests, docs or changelog
skip-unrequested-tests-docs.what: Adds a short APPEND_SYSTEM.md section: don't add tests, docs, changelog entries or features the request didn't ask for (offer them in the final message); verify with a throwaway /tmp script plus the existing tests covering the change; update only assertions encoding the old behavior; check failing tests against unchanged code (one-line git stash) and leave pre-existing failures alone.
skip-unrequested-tests-docs.why: Task messages are bare issues, yet 81/100 parent diffs touch tests (68 add test functions) and 31 touch docs/changelog, some with invented PR numbers. ~23% of output tokens come after the first test-file edit. In all 5 tasks where one run added tests and the other didn't, the test-adding run cost more (geo-mean 1.9x). Worst: matplotlib-23299 spent ~70 turns debugging its own test; django-16454 ~20k tokens wiring one into test infrastructure. Only ~2 of 25 code edits after test-writing came from a new test catching a bug.
skip-unrequested-tests-docs.expect: Fewer turns and output tokens on most fix/feature tasks (roughly 10-25%); verification still runs via scratch scripts and existing tests, so solves should hold. Text-only, no kick-in record. Small tries: 20-45% fewer turns; still wrote a test when asked.

startup-environment-facts.name: startup-environment-facts
startup-environment-facts.title: Tell the agent environment facts up front: python, tests, imports, net
startup-environment-facts.what: An extension probes the machine once at startup (~0.3 s) and adds a short <environment> section to the system prompt: the python in use and whether pytest is installed, the project's own test-runner script, whether `import <pkg>` loads the checkout or an installed copy (with a verified PYTHONPATH/sys.path fix), no network, no rg. When rg is missing, pi's 'ls, rg, find' rule says grep.
startup-environment-facts.why: The parent learns these by failing: 'No module named pytest' in 21/100 runs (sympy-20916 tried pytest twice before bin/test), 'rg: command not found' in 13 (pi's prompt recommends rg), pip/URL fetches in ~13, and in ~5 runs probes or the test runner imported an installed copy (django-7530 tested the egg, then patched it). These calls and their recovery turns cost ~5% of output tokens; shadowed imports verify the wrong code.
startup-environment-facts.expect: Right test command and import path on the first try; fewer failed setup calls and network attempts. Small token savings (a few %) on about half the tasks, fewer wrong-copy verifications, no added turns. Kicks in on every task; the acted record lists the facts stated.
